rationale: This is essentially an ensemble of two existing archive winners built from the same underlying `xrd` series, so the stated premise that their measurement errors are "partly independent" is unsupported — the level floor and the annual ramp are mechanically linked — and the likely outcome is an interpolation between two known alphas rather than new information.

The mechanical argument (intan inflates the ceq numerator, so the padding contaminates the ratio itself rather than merely correlating with it) is sound and makes this a legitimate grid-fill, but it substantially overlaps OrganicIntangibleValueTilt (same two ingredients, multiplicative rather than rank-difference form) which already failed at t=-1.23, so expected incremental value is modest.

`SUB(x, IND_ADJ(x))` cleanly isolates the between-industry component and converts the gen-3 demeaning result into a direct attribution test, which is genuinely diagnostic; the main caveat is that the commitment leg then varies only across a few dozen industries, so the FMB t-stat will be inflated by within-industry residual correlation and should be read with that discount.

The intangible-versus-tangible investment mix is a genuinely new channel and the industry-rank scaling of both halves is the right construction, but the `GROWTH(at,1)` half is the published asset-growth anomaly (partly absorbed by CMA in the FF5 alpha) and the reasoning misattributes a "magnitude flaw" to an earlier composition signal that actually worked (t=2.92), so the motivating diagnosis is shaky.

Deleting one `COALESCE(xad, 0)` term from an existing archive signal is the definition of a cosmetic variant, and since missing xad is already zero-filled the term cannot be contributing an "advertising-reporter tilt" in the way claimed — the coverage is identical (0.140), so the stated attribution problem is largely imaginary.

This ablation targets a structural assumption shared by nearly every archive winner — that R&D must enter both the value leg and the intangible leg — which makes it more informative than a typical single-term variant, though it reduces to plain B/M plus R&D-intensity, a pairing close to the published R&D-intensity-within-value literature, so a positive result would be hard to claim as novel.
